programme_name: Master's degree in Viticulture, enology and wine marketing (interuniversity)
campus: First year: Conegliano (University of Padua viticulture and enology campus); second year: Verona, Udine, or Conegliano depending on track. Administrative headquarters: Verona.

admission_routes.notes: Register in ESSE3 for the Eligibility Check from 3 June to 15 October 2026; late registration remains possible through 12 November 2026, followed by enrolment by 21 December 2026 with a late fee.
The ordinary ESSE3 Eligibility Check applies; applicants should verify residence-status documentation with the admissions office.

Foreign-degree holders of non-Italian citizenship who are not already resident in Italy apply through the 2026/27 International Master's pre-admission call, then complete Universitaly visa pre-enrolment if admitted.

academic_requirements.summary: A three-year university degree in viticulture and enology, or in agricultural sciences and/or food technology with appropriate preparation in plant production and protection, food technology, and economics. The ordinary programme requirement is met by an Italian L-25 or L-26 degree related to the wine sector, former class 20, or an old-system five-year Agricultural Sciences degree; otherwise at least 50 CFU in the specified subject groups are required. Curricular deficiencies must be remedied before enrolment. For the 2026/27 international pre-admission route, the qualifying degree must be awarded by 30 June 2026.
eligible_degree_classes: old-system five-year degree in Agricultural Sciences
academic_requirements.eligible_foreign_qualifications: A foreign first-cycle or higher degree recognised as suitable after assessment of whether its curriculum matches the programme's curricular and preparation requirements.

academic_requirements.minimum_grade_or_gpa: Ordinary entry: applicants with a graduation grade below 90/110 undergo a test or interview; those with 90/110 or higher are exempt. International scholarship/tuition-benefit eligibility requires CGPA or equivalent of at least 70/100.
academic_requirements.curriculum_assessment: The programme evaluates curricular requirements and personal preparation. For the international pre-admission call, academic background, relevant examination results, publications, extra-academic experience, institution profile, CGPA, English above B2, and an online interview are scored.

curricula_tracks.name: Economy and marketing in wine business
Research and development for a sustainable viticulture

ranking_and_quota.ranking_details: The degree itself is not presented as limited-entry. Under the separate 2026/27 international pre-admission and benefits call, applicants need at least 60/100; the programme ranking was to be published by 15 May 2026. One €8,000 scholarship plus tuition exemption was assigned to this programme, while the call also offered university-wide reduced-fee awards.

document_legalisation_translation_rules: Internationally pre-admitted applicants must submit an official translation and legalisation of the Bachelor's diploma plus a Declaration of Value. A CIMEA Statement of Comparability may replace the Declaration of Value, and a CIMEA Statement of Verification may replace legalisation.

entry_exam_or_test.mode: Online for the international pre-admission call; ordinary-route mode is not fully specified for 2026/27 [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test.minimum_score: International call: overall 60/100; interview contributes up to 30 points. Ordinary route: applicants with degree grade below 90/110, or without B2 certification, undergo a test/interview.
alternatives: Ordinary-route applicants with a degree grade of 90/110 or higher are exempt from the personal-preparation test/interview
B2 English may be assessed during an interview if certification is absent
entry_exam_or_test.notes: The international call states that applicants are informed of the pre-admission result within 45 days of application; its ranking was due by 15 May 2026. The programme page had not published 2026/27 ordinary interview dates in the material located.

application_fee.notes: Applies to the 2026/27 international pre-admission call. It is deducted from student contributions for those who enrol, except scholarship recipients.

tuition_amount_basis: General annual tuition rules apply. International students with a study visa or study residence permit may qualify for differentiated flat rates of €500 for applicants from World Bank low/lower-middle-income countries or €1,000 for applicants from upper-middle-income countries. The 2026/27 international call separately offered a €1,000 two-year reduced flat rate to selected non-EU applicants.

double_degree_options.notes: Eligible enrolled VEM students may complete the second year in Geisenheim and obtain both the Italian degree and the German MSc in Viticulture and Enology VITIS-VINUM. This mobility selection is separate from initial admission.

applicant_category_notes: The international pre-admission call is limited to non-Italian citizens (except dual-citizenship cases), holding a foreign degree and not already resident in Italy. EU/equivalent and non-EU applicants resident in Italy normally use the ordinary ESSE3 eligibility-check route. Universitaly is additionally mandatory for non-EU applicants abroad who need a study visa.
